stories.noticed: McDavid's 97.0 native result confirms that the model recognizes an elite NHL center before making any cross-sport comparison. Creation, scoring and discipline then provide the largest positive signals in a 96.1 guard comparison.
stories.logic: An attacking center carries play through transition, enters dangerous space and creates chances for teammates. A basketball guard also advances possession, organizes attacks and decides when to pass or finish, so the broad responsibility is easy to understand.
stories.caution: Elite hockey creation does not demonstrate dribbling, jump shooting or basketball defense. The comparison is strong because the shared statistical profile is strong, not because the sports use the same technique.

stories.noticed: Curry's 92.9 scoring and finishing profile is the main reason the right-wing comparison reaches 77.7. His body fit is only 18.3, which makes this a playing-style story rather than a physical one.
stories.logic: Curry creates separation without the ball, finds small shooting windows and turns quick releases into efficient scoring. Hockey wingers also rely on off-puck movement, timing and finishing before a defense can recover.
stories.caution: The low body score matters, and the model sees no skating, puck handling or contact along the boards. Similar scoring responsibilities do not make the underlying skills interchangeable.

stories.tag: A headline score that needs context
stories.noticed: LeBron's 93.8 native result is reassuring, but the 65.8 edge comparison is driven mainly by physical terms while the separate body-fit check is 0.0 and outside the usual target range.
stories.logic: His size, strength and ability to create force in transition make a defensive-football comparison tempting at a surface level. Both roles can reward acceleration, leverage and contact through crowded space.
stories.caution: The model also raises an age warning and does not measure pass-rush technique, block shedding or line-of-scrimmage movement. The body-fit disagreement is a reason to distrust the headline number.

stories.noticed: Wembanyama has a 96.7 native result, but the model withholds the tight-end comparison. His listed build falls outside the target reference and the target-role playing-profile model did not pass its own test.
stories.logic: Exceptional height and reach naturally suggest catch radius, red-zone targets and contested catches, which explains why a tight-end analogy comes to mind before the model is consulted.
stories.caution: An unusual body is not automatically a good fit. Blocking, route running, football contact and safe movement at that build are unmeasured, so showing no estimate is the responsible result.

stories.noticed: Jackson's body fit is only 17.4, yet the full guard comparison reaches 81.6. Scoring and creation are the two largest positive signals, showing how playing profile can change a body-only answer.
stories.logic: A quarterback and a guard both direct an offense, read movement ahead of them and create options while carrying the central object of play. Jackson also creates value through movement when the original play breaks down.
stories.caution: The model does not observe basketball shooting, dribbling or half-court defense. The strong profile score should be read beside the weak body comparison, not in place of it.

stories.tag: A plausible idea the model withholds
stories.noticed: Watt records a 77.2 native result, but the NHL-defense estimate is withheld. His build is outside the target reference and the target model did not show enough improvement to support the playing-profile comparison.
stories.logic: Pressure, contact, disruption and stopping attacks before they develop create a reasonable conceptual link between an edge defender and a hockey defenseman.
stories.caution: The model has no evidence for skating, backward movement, puck control or hockey positioning. A familiar defensive identity is not enough to justify a numeric transfer score.

stories.noticed: Haaland combines a 98.7 native result with an 87.6 guard comparison and an 80.4 body fit. Creation and scoring are both positive, so this is not being produced by size alone.
stories.logic: A forward times runs into gaps, receives under pressure and turns a small number of high-value chances into scores. An attacking guard also reads openings, drives into space and must decide quickly between creating and finishing.
stories.caution: Soccer movement does not prove ball handling, perimeter shooting or basketball defense. The model also uses broad public role labels, so the result is better for generating questions than naming a real position switch.

stories.tag: Typical build is not the whole answer
stories.noticed: Van Dijk's build is very typical for the broad guard comparison at 89.5, but the full score is a more moderate 66.7. Scoring helps while the model's creation measure pulls the estimate down.
stories.logic: A central defender reads play from deep, distributes into space and uses positioning to control transitions. Those ideas have a loose connection to a larger guard organizing possession and anticipating passing lanes.
stories.caution: A typical target build is not evidence of guard skill. The model cannot see dribbling, shooting touch, lateral quickness or how a football defender would move on a basketball court.

stories.noticed: Kempe's 90.7 native result establishes a strong NHL season. Creation and scoring lift the guard comparison to 69.0, while low discipline and a 40.4 body fit keep the cross-sport result more measured.
stories.logic: A scoring winger attacks in transition, moves the puck into dangerous areas and alternates between creating and finishing. Those broad choices resemble some of the responsibilities of an attacking guard.
stories.caution: The comparison says nothing about basketball handling, shooting mechanics or defensive footwork. It is also much less convincing than Kempe's native result, which should remain the main reference point.

stories.noticed: Johnston has the clearest mix of target-role build and playing profile in this set. His height sits comfortably within the NHL left-wing comparison, while scoring and finishing provide the strongest positive playing-style signal.
stories.logic: Wide receivers and hockey wingers both try to create separation, attack open space and turn a limited number of chances into meaningful gains. That makes the comparison understandable even though the techniques are completely different.
stories.caution: The data do not measure skating, puck handling, contact along the boards or hockey decision-making. This is a strong resemblance case—not evidence that Johnston could step onto NHL ice.

stories.noticed: This result is not driven by body type alone. Creation and distribution make the largest positive contribution, with discipline and scoring also helping the comparison.
stories.logic: A puck-moving defenseman helps start attacks, advances play through transition and distributes under pressure. Those responsibilities broadly resemble a basketball guard bringing the ball forward and organizing possessions.
stories.caution: Passing with a stick is not ball handling, and reading a hockey transition does not prove basketball court vision. The useful connection is the shared responsibility for creating and moving play.

stories.noticed: Johnson's build sits reasonably close to the midfielder comparison group. Scoring and finishing provide the largest positive playing-profile signal.
stories.logic: Receivers must find space, adjust their movement as a play develops and create value after receiving the ball. Those ideas loosely resemble a midfielder finding space and contributing during transitions.
stories.caution: Only a small number of performance themes connect these roles. The model does not observe soccer endurance, first touch, passing range or defensive positioning, so this is an interesting lead rather than a headline conclusion.

stories.noticed: The model's broad recovery and rebounding theme raises this comparison, and his listed build is not especially unusual for the target group.
stories.logic: Goalies react quickly, control rebounds and recover their position after an initial attempt. Basketball also rewards reactions to loose balls and rebounds, so the model has found a real shared theme.
stories.caution: The meaning of recovery is radically different for a goalie and a guard. This is better for explaining how the system finds statistical analogies than for suggesting a real transfer. The model also uses a frozen 2025 Boston snapshot, not his current team status.

stories.noticed: Kastelic's weight and defensive-disruption profile strongly raise the fitted comparison. His game also involves physical contact and competition through crowded areas, which creates an understandable surface-level connection with defensive football.
stories.logic: Both roles can reward contact, disruption and the ability to keep working through traffic. That shared physical identity explains why the model notices the comparison even though the movements are very different.
stories.caution: His body fit is weak and only broad playing themes connect the roles. The model does not measure pass-rush technique, block shedding, line-of-scrimmage stance or football-specific acceleration, so the high score needs prominent caution.
